elements.text: Loss of control due to sudden aileron hinge moment reversal after ice accreted beyond deice boots
ATR failed to disclose known effects of freezing precipitation on stability/control, autopilot procedures, and training
DGAC's inadequate oversight of ATR 42/72 and failure to ensure continued airworthiness in icing
DGAC's failure to provide timely airworthiness information to the FAA per Bilateral Agreement
FAA's failure to ensure certification and operational requirements accounted for hazards of freezing rain/icing not in Appendix C
FAA's inadequate oversight of ATR 42/72 to ensure continued airworthiness in icing
Flightcrew properly certified and qualified
ARTCC controllers properly certified and trained
ATR 72 certificated, equipped, and maintained per regulations
No evidence of aircraft structural or system failure
Encounter with rime/clear icing in supercooled cloud and large droplets
NWS forecasts were correct and actions in accordance with guidelines
HIWAS information presentation could be enhanced for safety
Flightcrew actions would not have differed with AIRMETs
Flightcrew actions consistent with training and knowledge
PIREPs may be misleading regarding icing severity
Ambiguity of 'icing in precipitation' phrase in aviation publications
Potential for improved atmospheric monitoring equipment and nowcasts
CFR Part 25 Appendix C envelope is limited and inadequate for all natural icing conditions
Recommendation against certifying for icing more severe than tested without demonstration
FAA inaction on 1981 icing recommendations may have prevented accident
ATR 42/72 susceptibility to aileron hinge moment reversal in freezing drizzle conditions
Control forces within standards but recovery difficult due to sudden onset and lack of warning/training
ATR considering design changes to reduce susceptibility to hinge moment reversals
DGAC and FAA failed to require documentation of undesirable post-SPS flight characteristics
Recommendation for test procedure to identify susceptibility to hinge moment reversals
ATR recognized cause of aileron behavior prior to accident and had basis for modification/warnings
1989 training simulator package did not provide training for hinge moment reversal recognition/recovery
ATR's proposed AFM/FCOM changes were insufficient for recovery
1992 ATR brochure was misleading and minimized catastrophic potential
ATR failed to disseminate adequate warnings/guidance and develop modifications, leading directly to accident
DGAC failed to require additional corrective actions, leading directly to accident
FAA's failure to require additional actions after 1994 incident contributed to accident
FAA AEG did not receive pertinent documentation timely
FAA AEG monitoring hampered by communication issues and DGAC failure to provide info
FAA's excessive reliance on foreign authority raises safety concerns
ATC release of flight was proper with viable avoidance options
Controllers acted appropriately in traffic management
ATC coordinator failure to report delay did not affect operation or contribute to accident
Controller conclusion of no significant weather was reasonable given lack of PIREPs
Lack of specific warnings about freezing rain effects left crew unaware of risks
Flight attendant presence and conversations did not contribute to accident
Flightcrew failure to increase RPM/activate ice protection was not a factor
Crew likely would have exited if they could observe ice buildup or had means to determine unsafe condition
Captain's departure from cockpit did not contribute to accident
Flightcrew failure to provide PIREP did not contribute to accident
